annotations.betterLine: Play Great Furnace first (or Mountain), then consider casting Palladium Myr with 3 mana (2 Mountains + Mind Stone) to accelerate into bigger plays next turn, or at minimum play the land before casting Epochrasite to keep options open.

annotations.description: Discarding Epochrasite over a basic Mountain is a mistake. With 2 Mountains already on the battlefield plus Great Furnace and Temple of the False God in hand, Johnny has plenty of red mana sources. Epochrasite is a useful artifact creature that synergizes with Daretti (the commander) and artifact sacrifice themes - it even comes back from dying with +1/+1 counters via suspend. A basic Mountain is far less valuable than a reusable artifact creature in this deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Epochrasite to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard a basic Mountain instead, keeping Epochrasite as a useful artifact creature that synergizes with the artifact-focused commander deck and has built-in recursion when it dies.

annotations.description: Orzhov Basilica enters tapped and requires bouncing a land, costing tempo. With Commander's Sphere already providing color fixing and only 4 lands on board, Exotic Orchard or Blighted Woodland would have been better choices. Exotic Orchard enters untapped and can produce any color opponents' lands make (which covers all colors given the diverse mana bases). Blighted Woodland enters untapped and provides ramp later. The Basilica bounce-land is slow and GPT52 is already behind on board development at turn 6.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Orzhov Basilica from Satyr Wayfinder's trigger
annotations.betterLine: Select Exotic Orchard for an untapped land that provides immediate color fixing, or Blighted Woodland for future ramp potential without the tempo loss of bouncing a land.

annotations.description: Discarded Palladium Myr (a 3-mana ramp artifact that taps for {C}{C}) instead of one of three redundant Mountains in hand. With Daretti as commander, Palladium Myr provides meaningful ramp and could also be recurred from the graveyard, but keeping it in hand is strictly better than a third Mountain when you already have Great Furnace and Temple of the False God as additional land drops.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Palladium Myr to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the three Mountains in hand, keeping the ramp creature that taps for 2 mana

annotations.description: Johnny has 8 cards in hand and will need to discard to 7 at end of turn. By tapping Mind Stone for colorless mana during combat (which appears to go unused), they gain nothing and still have to discard. They could have instead sacrificed Mind Stone to draw a card (paying {1} from the colorless mana plus tapping it), which would have been card-neutral but let them see a new card and choose what to discard from a better selection. With 3 Mountains untapped plus Mind Stone, they had exactly the mana to activate the sacrifice ability ({1} + {T}). Instead they just tapped it for mana that floated away unused and had to discard Liquimetal Coating.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Mind Stone for {C} during combat, mana went unused, then discarded Liquimetal Coating to hand size.
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Mind Stone to draw a card (pay {1} from a Mountain, tap and sacrifice Mind Stone). This cycles through the deck and gives better selection on the discard, rather than wasting the Mind Stone's sacrifice ability while being forced to discard anyway.

annotations.description: GPT5n Johnny tapped Mind Stone for colorless mana during the combat phase but had no apparent use for it - no instant-speed abilities or spells to cast with the mana. The mana will be wasted. More importantly, with 8 cards in hand and needing to discard to 7, they should have sacrificed Mind Stone to draw a card instead of just tapping for mana. Sacrificing Mind Stone would have drawn a card (net neutral on hand size since they'd still discard to 7, but they'd get card selection) and also put an artifact in the graveyard which could matter. They ended up discarding Faithless Looting anyway, so the draw would have given them a chance to see a better card and choose what to discard.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Mind Stone for {C} during combat with no use for the mana, then discarded Faithless Looting to hand size.
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Mind Stone to draw a card ({1}, {T}, Sacrifice), getting card selection before discarding to hand size. This converts the Mind Stone into a fresh card while still going to 7 cards in hand.

annotations.description: Johnny is completely mana-flooded with a hand of 8 lands (needing to discard to 7). Tapping Mind Stone for {C} during combat produces mana that goes completely unused since there's nothing to spend it on. They already have 3+ untapped Mountains plus Mind Stone itself.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Mind Stone for {C} mana that went unused
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Mind Stone to draw a card ({1}, {T}, Sacrifice: Draw a card) using one of the three untapped Mountains to pay {1}. When completely flooded with all lands in hand, converting a mana rock into card draw is essential to find action.

annotations.description: Cairn Wanderer is a 4/4 changeling that gains keyword abilities from creature cards in graveyards. With Zetalpa (flying, double strike, vigilance, trample, indestructible) and Skullwinder (deathtouch) already in GPT52's own graveyard, plus creatures in opponents' graveyards, Cairn Wanderer would be an extremely powerful creature if cast. Meanwhile, Soulflayer could also benefit from delving Zetalpa, but Cairn Wanderer doesn't require exiling the graveyard cards — it checks all graveyards continuously. Discarding Cairn Wanderer removes a castable 5-mana threat that would have flying, double strike, vigilance, trample, indestructible, and deathtouch. A better discard would be Martial Impetus (a situational aura) or Exotic Orchard (an extra land when they already have 5 mana sources plus Commander's Sphere). Soulflayer is the card that wants graveyard creatures to be exiled with delve, making it somewhat redundant with Unburial Rites strategy, so discarding Soulflayer could also be considered over Cairn Wanderer.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Cairn Wanderer
annotations.betterLine: Discard Martial Impetus or Exotic Orchard instead, preserving Cairn Wanderer as a powerful creature that would gain flying, double strike, vigilance, trample, indestructible, and deathtouch from Zetalpa and Skullwinder in graveyard

annotations.description: Casting Mnemonic Sphere for 2 mana to later sacrifice it for 2 more mana (total 4 mana for 2 cards) versus channeling it now for U (1 mana for 1 card). The channel option is more mana-efficient per card drawn. However, casting it has synergy with Kimi25 Vet's artifact-matters cards (Fain, the Broker and Farid, Enterprising Salvager), so putting it on the battlefield as an artifact that can be sacrificed for value later is reasonable. The player also has Spine of Ish Sah in hand (7 mana) and needs to develop, so spending 2 mana now to deploy an artifact that draws 2 cards later (and can be sacrificed to Fain/Farid for additional value) is defensible. This is close to reasonable given the artifact synergies on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mnemonic Sphere for {1}{U} to put it on the battlefield as an artifact
annotations.betterLine: Given the artifact synergies with Fain and Farid on the battlefield, casting is defensible. However, channeling for U and using the remaining mana to cast Nihil Spellbomb (another artifact for synergy, plus graveyard hate against opponents with stacked graveyards like GPT52 Villain's Zetalpa and Soul of Innistrad) could have been more impactful.

annotations.description: Tapping Mind Stone for colorless mana during combat with nothing to spend it on - the mana will go to waste. Given a hand full of lands and needing to discard, sacrificing Mind Stone to draw a card could have found action, though losing the mana rock is a real cost. At minimum, the tap for mana accomplished nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Mind Stone for {C} during combat, generating mana that went unused
annotations.betterLine: Either sacrifice Mind Stone to draw a card (hand is all lands, desperate for action) or simply don't activate it during combat. Sacrificing seems better given the land-flooded hand and the fact that Mind Stone's mana is less needed with 6+ lands in hand.

annotations.description: GPT5n Johnny is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Great Furnace, an artifact land, over a basic Mountain. With Epochrasite and other artifacts already in the graveyard, and playing a Daretti/artifact-themed deck, Great Furnace in play would be strictly better than a basic Mountain since it counts as an artifact for synergies (Daretti's -2, Slobad, etc.) while still producing red mana. Meanwhile, they have 4+ basic Mountains in hand that are functionally worse. Discarding a basic Mountain would preserve the option to play the artifact land later.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Great Furnace instead of a basic Mountain
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the multiple basic Mountains in hand, keeping Great Furnace as the superior land to play in future turns for artifact synergies with Daretti

annotations.description: Tapping Mind Stone for colorless mana during combat with nothing useful to spend it on, when the hand is flooded with lands (5 Mountains, Temple, Ghost Quarter) and will need to discard. annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Mind Stone for {C} during combat, wasting the mana and keeping a less useful permanent
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Mind Stone to draw a card ({1}, {T}, Sacrifice), getting a chance to find action while discarding excess lands

annotations.description: GPT5n Johnny is discarding to hand size (8 cards, max 7). They have 4 lands on the battlefield and several lands in hand. Reliquary Tower provides no maximum hand size, which would have prevented this exact discard situation in future turns. Additionally, Reliquary Tower produces colorless mana which is less useful than the other utility lands. However, the real issue is that they should be discarding a basic Mountain instead - they have 3 Mountains in hand and 3 on the battlefield already. Reliquary Tower has unique utility (no max hand size) and also taps for colorless, while a 6th Mountain is redundant. Ghost Quarter has removal utility, Temple of the False God produces double mana, Commander's Sphere and Pristine Talisman are mana rocks they still need to cast. Discarding a Mountain would preserve optionality.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Reliquary Tower, losing the unique no-maximum-hand-size utility land.
annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the three Mountains in hand, as they already have 3 Mountains on the battlefield and the extra Mountain is far more redundant than Reliquary Tower's unique ability.

annotations.description: GPT52 Villain discarded Mimic Vat, a powerful artifact that synergizes extremely well with their graveyard-heavy strategy. They have numerous creatures in their graveyard (Zetalpa, Soul of Innistrad, Vampire Nighthawk, Skullwinder, etc.) and Mimic Vat would let them imprint dying creatures to repeatedly generate token copies. With only 5 mana sources and needing land drops, discarding a land like Memorial to Folly (which enters tapped and has a narrow ability they may not need) or Exotic Orchard would have been more appropriate. Alternatively, Soulflayer could be discarded since it's a 6-mana creature that requires careful graveyard management for its delve ability, and many of the keyword creatures are already in the graveyard where they'd be better served by other reanimation effects. Mimic Vat at 3 mana is very castable and provides repeatable value.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Mimic Vat
annotations.betterLine: Discard Memorial to Folly or Exotic Orchard instead, keeping Mimic Vat which is a high-value 3-mana artifact that provides repeatable creature token generation from dying creatures, synergizing with the board state where multiple creatures are trading.

annotations.description: Johnny tapped Mind Stone for mana during combat when they have no creatures to attack with and could have sacrificed it to draw a card instead. They have a land drop available (4 Mountains in hand) which would give them enough mana (4 Mountains = enough for a 3-drop like Commander's Sphere or Pristine Talisman) even after sacrificing Mind Stone. Drawing a card would have been strictly better than the colorless mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Mind Stone for {C} during combat
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Mind Stone to draw a card ({1}, {T}, sacrifice), then in main phase 2 play a Mountain from hand and still have 3 Mountains available to cast Commander's Sphere or Pristine Talisman.

annotations.betterLine: Discard one of the four Mountains in hand, keeping Commander's Sphere as a valuable mana rock and card-draw source for a mana-starved board position.

Playing Fellwar Stone accelerates toward Hellkite Igniter or Master Transmuter next turn. annotations.betterLine: Cast Fellwar Stone (2 mana) and Nihil Spellbomb (1 mana) to develop the board. Could also play the Swamp from hand for the land drop if it wasn't already played this turn, further enabling future plays.

Kimi25 has no creatures on board and no way to attack, but they skipped attacking AND failed to deploy threats when they could have. More critically, they have Bedevil in hand which cannot destroy Zetalpa (indestructible), but they have Nihil Spellbomb which could exile an opponent's graveyard. The key issue is skipping the attack step is fine (no creatures), but the reasoning mentions 'Spine ends this' which doesn't exist in their hand or board - they seem confused about their available cards. They should have cast Nihil Spellbomb (1 mana) and Fellwar Stone (2 mana) to develop their board, and potentially cast Master Transmuter to start building toward their artifact synergies. Playing just a land and passing with 5+ mana available and multiple castable spells is a significant tempo loss when facing a Zetalpa that threatens to kill them.

annotations.description: Gem3P Stoic is at 8 life and has Zetalpa on board as the only real threat. Kimi25 Vet has Bedevil in hand which can destroy Zetalpa (or any creature/artifact/planeswalker), but instead cast Trading Post, a slow value engine. Meanwhile, Stoic's Zetalpa is indestructible so Bedevil can't actually destroy it - but more importantly, Kimi25 Vet has Geth, Lord of the Vault in hand (costs 4BB) and has access to enough mana lands to potentially cast it. With GPT52 Villain's massive graveyard full of powerful creatures (Cairn Wanderer, Cataclysmic Gearhulk, Archon of Valor's Reach, Vampire Nighthawk, etc.), Geth would be an extremely powerful play. However, looking at available mana - Kimi25 has Shadowblood Ridge, Mountain, Drossforge Bridge, Island, Reliquary Tower, Machine God's Effigy, Myriad Landscape, Ichor Wellspring - that's only about 6-7 mana sources and Geth costs 4BB which requires two black. The real issue is that Nihil Spellbomb should have been considered to exile GPT52 Villain's graveyard (preventing Stoic from using those resources) or as setup. Trading Post is a 4-mana do-nothing this turn when the game state calls for more impactful plays. Fellwar Stone + Nihil Spellbomb would have been better mana development while keeping interaction available.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Trading Post (4 mana artifact with slow activated abilities)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fellwar Stone (2 mana) for ramp plus Nihil Spellbomb (1 mana) as graveyard interaction, or cast Fellwar Stone plus hold up Bedevil mana for interaction, setting up to cast Geth next turn with proper mana development.
